deities: Goddess Chamundi (Maha Chamundi, calm form, main sanctum - panchaloha idol of Karikkakathamma, an incarnation of Parvati)
Raktha Chamundi (fierce form; wall painting in Rowdra Bhava, no vigraha)
Bala Chamundi (childhood form, worshipped by couples seeking children)

history.dynasty: Travancore (during the Maharajas' rule the temple served as a place where justice and truth were tested; the place was once a kalari of Travancore soldiers, hence Kalarikkakom, abbreviated to Karikkakom)
history.period: More than 600 years old per temple tradition (antiquity attributed by astrologers and older generations; exact founding date unknown)
history.summary: The Karikkakom Sree Chamundi Devi Temple is an ancient Goddess temple about 7 km north of Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, famed for enshrining a panchaloha (five-metal: gold, copper, lead, silver and iron) idol of Karikkakathamma. Chamundi Devi is worshipped here in three adjacent forms: calm Maha Chamundi in the main sanctum, fierce Raktha Chamundi (a wall painting in Rowdra Bhava, with no idol), and child-form Bala Chamundi. During the Travancore kings' rule the temple was a venue of justice: accused persons proved their innocence by the Satyam Thellikkal ritual - standing before Raktha Chamundi's nada, placing 21 coins (panam) and swearing to tell the truth, in the belief that the Devi would protect the truthful and punish liars; the nada opens only for this ritual. A nagar kavu (sacred grove) with trees and medicinal plants lies outside the temple wall. NOTE: several sources describe the temple timings inconsistently (one lists an implausible 5:00 AM-12:00 midnight daily; another 4:30-8:00 AM) - verify darshan hours locally before visiting.

name: Karikkakom Sree Chamundi Devi Temple
town_description: Thiruvananthapuram is the capital of Kerala; the temple stands in the Karikkakom locality, about 7 km north of the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple (Kizhakkekotta/East Fort area), within the city.

travel.airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, the nearest airport - verify road distance locally.
travel.railway: Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station, about 7 km away.
travel.road: Located in the Karikkakom area of Thiruvananthapuram city, reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw or taxi from East Fort (Kizhakkekotta).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather; festival days such as Pongala and Makam draw large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict (one lists 4:30-8:00 AM daily; another an implausible all-day schedule) - verify locally before visiting. As with most Kerala temples, expect a morning and an evening session with a midday break.
